name: TrueProof
author: TrueProof

sections.description:
TrueProof turns the real activity on your site into social proof that converts. It shows tasteful notification bubbles of genuine recent orders, signups and reviews — automated word-of-mouth that helps new visitors trust you.

Brand-new site with no traffic yet? Use Simulation Mode to design, preview and test your notifications with clearly-labelled sample data, then flip to Real Data Mode the moment your first customers arrive.

Honest by design

  • Real Data Mode pulls genuine events from WooCommerce, Easy Digital Downloads, user registrations and approved comments/reviews.
  • Simulation Mode is for previewing only and always shows a visible “Demo” badge — your visitors are never misled.
  • Built to respect FTC and EU rules on endorsements and testimonials.

Features

  • WooCommerce & Easy Digital Downloads integration
  • New-user registration and recent-review notifications
  • Name anonymisation (e.g. “Anna K.”) for GDPR-friendly display
  • Lightweight vanilla-JavaScript frontend — fast, no jQuery, no layout shift
  • Position, accent colour, timing and per-page display controls
  • Results cached server-side; events served over the REST API
  • No external services, no tracking, no phone-home, no ads

Privacy

TrueProof only reads data that already exists on your own site (orders, users, comments) and never sends anything to third parties. Displayed names can be anonymised to first name + initial. See the FAQ for the exact data shown.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the trueproof folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install via Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings → TrueProof, choose your mode (start with Simulation), pick your data sources, and save.
sections.faq:
Does it show fake data?

Only if you explicitly enable Simulation Mode, which always displays a visible “Demo” badge. Real Data Mode shows only genuine events from your own site.

What exactly is shown to visitors?

A first name (optionally anonymised to first name + initial), an optional city/country, the action (e.g. “purchased …”, “signed up”, “left a review”) and a relative time. No emails, no full addresses, no order totals.

Does it slow my site down?

No. The frontend is a tiny vanilla-JS script and events are cached server-side for a few minutes.

Is it GDPR-friendly?

Yes. Names can be anonymised, only first-party data is used, and nothing is sent to third parties.

Does it require WooCommerce?

No. WooCommerce and EDD are optional sources. Without them you can still show new registrations, comments/reviews, or Simulation Mode.
